**Ghostdrop v0.2.0** brings full Linux support (Wayland and X11 with zero-copy GPU presentation), major macOS and Linux stability hardening, and a unified cross-platform install/update flow.

### Highlights

- **Linux support (Wayland + X11).** A native Rust frontend on full [libghostty](https://github.com/ghostty-org/ghostty) (OpenGL renderer, FreeType/HarfBuzz/fontconfig, same `~/.config/ghostdrop/config`) with zero-copy DMA-BUF presentation (X11 DRI3/Present, Wayland `linux-dmabuf`), fractional scaling (`wp_fractional_scale_v1`), per-display control sockets, and an Arch `PKGBUILD` (`make pkg`).
- **Portable Linux releases.** Prebuilt `x86_64` and `aarch64` tarballs built against `glibc 2.35` (`ubuntu:22.04`) that run across Ubuntu 22.04+, Debian 12+, Fedora, Arch, and openSUSE.
- **Cross-platform `make install` and `make update`.** OS-aware `Makefile` works on both macOS and Linux. On Linux, `make install` downloads and verifies a prebuilt release tarball on release tags (or with `RELEASE=latest`) and falls back to building from source (`make deps` installs distro build packages; `clang`/`bindgen` is no longer required).
- **macOS deadlock fix and FFI isolation.** Fixed a main-thread self-deadlock on `libghostty`'s `renderer_state.mutex` triggered when clicking untrusted links (e.g. OSC 8 `file://`). All `libghostty` calls on both macOS and Linux now go through a single isolated FFI boundary with runtime re-entrancy guards, pure-data async callbacks, async clipboard reads, and exact-once clipboard request cleanup.
- **Explicit state machines & hardening.**
  - macOS: unified exact-once sheet prompt queue (close tab, quit, rename, clipboard, untrusted URL), zero post-launch `NSAlert.runModal()` calls, explicit show/hide/search/secure-input state, and a live macOS CI regression suite (`make test`).
  - Linux: explicit pointer-capture, prompt-queue, key-routing, autohide, and Wayland keyboard-interactivity state machines; bounded IPC read/write timeouts and size caps; async-signal-safe `eventfd` signal handling; and timeout escape hatches for hung clipboard owners and lost frame/DMA-BUF callbacks on both X11 and Wayland.

### Install

#### macOS (Apple Silicon, macOS 13+)

1. Download **`Ghostdrop-0.2.0.dmg`** below, open it, and drag **Ghostdrop** onto **Applications**.
2. Builds are ad-hoc signed (not notarized): on first launch use **System Settings -> Privacy & Security -> Open Anyway**.

#### Linux (`x86_64` / `aarch64`, glibc >= 2.35)

```sh
git clone https://github.com/HackToHell/ghostdrop && cd ghostdrop
make install RELEASE=v0.2.0    # downloads + verifies tarball into ~/.local
make update                    # git pull + reinstall
```

Or download **`ghostdrop-0.2.0-linux-<arch>.tar.gz`** below and extract into `~/.local`, or on Arch Linux run `make pkg`.

### Verify downloads

```sh
# macOS
shasum -a 256 -c Ghostdrop-0.2.0.dmg.sha256

# Linux
sha256sum -c ghostdrop-0.2.0-linux-x86_64.tar.gz.sha256
sha256sum -c ghostdrop-0.2.0-linux-aarch64.tar.gz.sha256
```
